variables_mentioned: IND (Income), accessed as INDH and INDK

registers.role: linkage: family/household linkages for matching spouses and cohabiting partners

registers.name_in_paper: Hustande og familier (Households and Families) (Statistics Denmark 2020c)
Integrated Database for Labor Market Research (Statistics Denmark 2020d)
registers.role: outcomes and controls: demographic variables for the entire population and administrative full-time/part-time employment measures for individuals younger than the early retirement age of 60, constructed from payments to the government-mandated ATP pension scheme
variables_mentioned: full-time employment (at least 30 hours per week all 12 months)

linkages: individual-level records with household linkages that allow spouses and cohabiting partners to be matched, 1980 to 2011
health events of one spouse linked to the labor market outcomes of the other spouse within the household
widows linked to their pre-event municipality of residence for the Social DI leave-one-out instrument

sample.universe: the universe of Danish married and cohabiting couples, 1980-2011, in which one spouse experienced a fatal or severe nonfatal health event between 1985 and 2011
sample.unit_of_observation: household-year (households indexed by time relative to the event, t = year - tau)
selection_rules: all households in which one spouse experienced an event from year 1985 to 2011
main (fatal) sample: households in which one spouse died and was between ages 45 and 80 in the year of the (actual or placebo) event
secondary (nonfatal) sample: households in which one spouse experienced a heart attack or a stroke for the first time and survived for at least three years
nonfatal sample further restricted to households with both spouses under 60, to avoid eligibility for early retirement benefits
control groups are households from the same cohorts experiencing the same event five years later (Delta = 5), with a placebo event assigned at t = 0
only households that experience the event at some point in the sample period are used; unaffected households are not used as controls
a household may appear in both the treatment and the control group, but is never used as a control to itself
sample.n_observations: fatal-event regressions: 1,397,030 observations for widowers and 2,919,946 for widows (household income: 1,396,657 and 2,919,243); nonfatal-shock regressions: 521,609 observations
sample.n_individuals: fatal events: 310,720 treatment and 409,190 control households (166,703 widower and 335,670 widow clusters); nonfatal shocks: 35,143 treatment and 52,196 control households (67,749 clusters)

construction_notes: labor force participation is defined as having any positive level of annual earnings; for individuals younger than the early retirement age of 60 an administrative any-employment measure based on the ATP-derived full-time/part-time measures is used

full-time employment is working at least 30 hours per week all 12 months of the calendar year; part-time employment is working at some point during the year but either fewer than 30 hours per week or fewer than 12 months

in the year of spousal death, the deceased's prorated earnings from that year (based on their month of death), which Statistics Denmark books to the surviving spouse, are subtracted from the survivor's annual earnings
all monetary values are in Danish Kroner deflated to 2000 prices using the consumer price index; the 2000 exchange rate was approximately 8 DKK per US$1
annual earnings include zeros for those who do not work
overall potential household income fixes the surviving spouse's labor income, Social Disability and Social Security benefits at their t = -1 level
in the figures the control group's outcome level is normalized to the pre-event level of the treatment group's outcome in period t = -2
Delta = 5, so effects are identified up to four years after the event; period 0 is a transitional year and period 1 the first fully exposed period
shock severity for nonfatal events is defined by the 75th percentile of hospitalization days associated with the shock (10 days)
